items.summary: पत्रकार रवि नायर को एक बार फिर कोई राहत नहीं मिली और वह फिलहाल जेल में ही रहेंगे. गुजरात हाईकोर्ट ने सोमवार को उनकी गिरफ्तारी चुनौती देने वाली याचिका पर अडाणी एंटरप्राइजेज को जवाब दाखिल करने का समय दे दिया. हालांकि, कोर्ट ने साफ कहा कि अडाणी एंटरप्राइजेज को यह आखिरी मौका है और इसके बाद आगे कोई स्थगन नहीं मिलेगा. अब मामले की अगली सुनवाई 23 सितंबर को होगी. मालूम हो कि रवि एक स्वतंत्र पत्रकार हैं. उन्होंने अडाणी-हिंडनबर्ग विवाद, कॉर्पोरेट एकाधिकार और कथित गलत कामों पर लगातार रिपोर्टिंग की है. लाइव लॉ की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, जस्टिस एम के ठक्कर की अदालत में अडाणी की ओर से पेश वकील ने कुछ कानूनी और तथ्यात्मक पहलू रिकॉर्ड पर लाने के लिए समय मांगा. नायर के वकील अभिक चिमनी ने इसका विरोध किया और अंतरिम राहत की मांग की. उन्होंने कहा कि मामला अपील स्तर पर है और एक निजी शिकायतकर्ता को बार-बार स्थगन नहीं मिलना चाहिए. साथ ही उन्होंने दलील दी कि उनके मुवक्किल (नायर) को एक दिन भी जेल में नहीं बिताना चाहिए. इस बीच अदालत ने नोटिस जारी होने के बाद शिकायतकर्ता को अपना पक्ष रखने का मौका देना उचित माना, लेकिन साथ ही कहा कि वह मामले में आगे कोई स्थगन नहीं होगा. मालूम हो कि रवि नायर को 17 सितंबर को गांधीनगर सत्र न्यायालय ने गैर-जमानती वारंट रद्द करने की अर्जी खारिज करने के बाद न्यायिक हिरासत में भेज दिया था

items.title: How Humayun landed a PSC candidate before Supreme Court over one mark
items.summary: The Supreme Court was recently called to decide a dispute over the answer to a question that had Mughal emperor Humayun and the Humayunnama as one of the answer options in a State recruitment exam [ UPSSSC v. Ashok Yadav ]. The dispute arose from a 2016 examination conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Service Selection Commission (UPSSSC) for recruitment to 3,133 posts of Village Development Officer. One of the general knowledge questions asked candidates to identify the incorrectly matched pair from the following options: Baburnama–Babur, Shahjahannama–Mohammad Tahir, Humayunnama–Humayun and Tuzuk-e-Jahangiri–Jahangir. The Commission treated “Shahjahannama–Mohammad Tahir” as the correct answer to the question. The UPSSC's basis for choosing the right pair was subject-wise pairing: matching each book with the person it is about. A candidate, however, selected “Humayunnama–Humayun” as the answer, since Humayunnama was authored by Gulbadan Begum and not Humayun. The remaining options matched the books to their authors. items.title: Delhi High Court notifies new rules for Senior Advocate designation; conduct, ethics, pro bono work made factors
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has notified new rules for the designation of lawyers as Senior Advocates, replacing the framework issued in March 2024. As per the new rules, an advocate's fairness, courtroom conduct, professional ethics, role as a mentor to junior advocates, pro bono work and standing in the legal fraternity will be taken into account while considering conferment of gown. Pertinently, the new rules have done away with the committee for designating Senior Advocates which was provided under the earlier rules. Under the new rules, a permanent secretariat headed by an officer of the rank of registrar will oversee the designation process and the designation will be decided directly by the full court. The secretariat will initiate the process at least once every year by inviting applications, with the notice to be published on the High Court's website and communicated to the Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA). Applicants will be given at least 21 days to apply. An advocate must ordinarily have at least 10 years of practice, should be enrolled with a Bar Council and should have mainly practised before the High Court, trial and district courts or specialised tribunals. items.title: Delhi High Court's working strength rises to 50 after 7 new judges take oath
items.summary: With the swearing-in of seven news judges on Monday, the Delhi High Court has received a significant boost to its working strength. The addition of the seven judges has taken the High Court's working strength to 50 against its sanctioned strength of 60 judges. This could be the first time the High Court is functioning with 50 sitting judges after its sanctioned strength was raised to 60 in 2014. In 2022, the working strength of the High Court had risen to 47 . With 83% of its sanctioned strength now functioning, the High Court, which has witnessed a continuous increase in the number of commercial matters, will have more judges to handle cases and improve its disposal rate. Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya today administered oath of office to Justices Nivedita Anil Sharma , Nisha Sahay Saxena , Sanjay Sharma , Bharat Parashar , Aditi Choudhary , Dinesh Bhatt and Arun Bhardwaj . The High Court now has 13 women judges. It will maintain the current strength of judges till next month, unless more judges are appointed. Four judges are slated to retire this year. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to issue a Red Corner Notice through Interpol to trace an individual called Adeeshwar Singhal who is accused of making scandalous allegations against the judiciary [ Court On Its Own Motion Vs Adeeshwar Singhal ]. The Division Bench of Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Ravinder Dudeja passed the order to secure Singhal’s physical presence in court in suo motu contempt of court proceedings initiated against him. “We direct the Central Bureau of Investigation to issue a Red Corner Notice through INTERPOL against the respondent (Singhal) for securing his presence in compliance of our orders, including the non-bailable warrants (NBWs),” the Court directed. On September 18, Singhal joined the Court proceedings through video conference and engaged in disruptive conduct. "We will ensure that you come to court, don’t think we will leave you like this. You are making a mockery of the proceedings and making allegations. Either you come here or we will get you here," Justice Chawla warned. items.title: First time court appearance: What not to do
items.summary: We all carry our fair share of courtroom mishaps, particularly from the early years. While mistakes can happen at any stage of the litigation career, the shaking and trembling hits very differently to the newly robed, often accompanied by a strong conviction that the legal career is over and it’s time to relocate to another country. To celebrate these mandatory rites of passage, I polled my litigation circle and discovered these gems. 1. During my first year, I was sent to seek a simple passover before a Supreme Court bench with clear instructions to say “my senior is on his legs in another courtroom”. But of course, appearing before a Supreme Court bench, my overwhelm got the better of me and being painfully honest, I blurted out, “my senior is on his legs in the NCLT” . At this point, I was not aware of the unwritten rule of forum hierarchy. I got a well-deserved chewing out from my senior at this point. - 23 y/o advocate assisting a well sought after criminal lawyer in Delhi. 2. items.title: Rape on promise of marriage: Surat lawyer withdraws plea in Gujarat HC to quash case filed by woman advocate
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court on September 17 allowed Surat-based advocate to withdraw his plea seeking the quashing of a rape case against him. Justice MK Thakker disposed off the petition after the accused-lawyer sought permission to withdraw it. "This Court has not gone into the merits of the matter," the judge clarified. Justice MK Thakker The lawyer is accused of establishing sexual relationship with a woman advocate after giving her a false promise of marriage. The accused had also sought anticipatory bail before the trial court in connection with the FIR. However, sources told Bar and Bench that the trial court had rejected this plea. The case arose from an eight-year-long relationship between the two advocates. According to the complainant, the relationship began in 2018 and allegedly continued until she learnt about the advocate's (petitioner's) marriage to another woman in March 2026. The complainant denied that their relationship was simply consensual as portrayed by the accused. items.title: UAPA property attachment: Delhi High Court says appeal against special judge order maintainable before HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that an appeal against a special judge's decision upholding attachment of property under Section 25(6) of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) is maintainable before the High Court [Aquil Ahmed v National Investigation Agency Throught the Chief Investigating Officer] . A Division Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja rejected the National Investigation Agency's (NIA) preliminary objection that a second appeal against an order of attachment was not maintainable. The NIA had said that Section 25(6) of the UAPA provides for only one appeal – to the special court. It also argued that Section 28 of UAPA separately provides for an appeal to the High Court against an eventual forfeiture order under Section 26. However, the Court said that forfeiture under Section 26 is a distinct action requiring a separate show-cause notice under Section 27. "Simple attachment of the property does not automatically lead to its forfeiture under Section 26 of the UAPA. items.title: J&K High Court stays FIR against woman booked for terminating pregnancy without husband’s consent
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh has stayed criminal investigation into a complaint filed by a husband alleging that his wife terminated a 4–5-month pregnancy without his consent, allegedly with the assistance of her sister. Justice Rahul Bharti passed the interim order on a plea by the accused (the complainant's wife and her sister) to quash the first information report (FIR) registered against them. Justice Rahul Bharti The FIR against the two accused cited Section 126(2) (wrongful restraint/confinement), Section 88 (causing miscarriage), Section 351(2) (criminal intimidation), Section 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and Section 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. In an order passed on September 14, however, the Court expressed reservations about the FIR, expressing a prima facie observation that the allegations did not inspire confidence. "The tone and tenor of the contents of the FIR on the face of it do not inspire confidence about the narrative being set up by the respondent No. 3 (complainant-husband) against the petitioner No. 1 (complainant's wife/ accused)," the Court said.
